title: Jobs
description: What is running, what is queued, and why it is stuck. The CoreWeave panels read the iris.task_state rollups the cluster-view controllers emit every 30s; the GCE controllers emit none and are queried live instead.

list.name: cluster
list.label: Cluster
list.description: The clusters the bridge serves (infra/grafana/src/config.py). A custom list rather than a query so a cluster that has gone silent -- exactly when you want to select it -- is still in the dropdown.

list.name: job
list.label: Job
list.description: Root jobs with task-state rows inside the dashboard window.

params.value: SELECT DISTINCT root_job_id AS value FROM "iris.task_state" WHERE root_job_id <> '' AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}} ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Provisioning failures
panels.description: Slice provisioning attempts that ended in stockout or error over the dashboard window. A wall of these is capacity, not code.

params.value: SELECT COUNT(*) AS value FROM "iris.provisioning" WHERE outcome IN ('stockout', 'error') AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}}

panels.title: Warning events
panels.description: Warning task events across the selected clusters over the dashboard window, summed with their repeat counts.

params.value: SELECT SUM(count) AS value FROM "iris.task_event" WHERE type = 'Warning' AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}}

panels.title: Fleet task states
panels.description: Every CoreWeave task in the selected clusters, stacked by state. The shape tells you which stage is the bottleneck: a thick pending band is scheduling, a thick building band is image pulls and setup.

params.value: WITH per_cluster AS ( SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', ts) AS t, COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') AS cl, MAX(pending) AS pending, MAX(assigned) AS assigned, MAX(building) AS building, MAX(running) AS running FROM "iris.task_state" WHERE root_job_id = '' AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}} GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT t, SUM(pending) AS pending, SUM(assigned) AS assigned, SUM(building) AS building, SUM(running) AS running FROM per_cluster GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Oldest waiting task by cluster
panels.description: How long the longest-waiting pending or building task has been waiting. This is the queue-pain number the stuck-job alert watches.

params.value: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', ts) AS t, COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') AS series, MAX(GREATEST(oldest_pending_age_ms, oldest_building_age_ms)) AS value FROM "iris.task_state" WHERE root_job_id = '' AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}} GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Provisioning attempts by outcome
panels.description: Every slice the autoscaler tried to create, by outcome. A stockout wall is the cloud saying no; errors are ours.

params.value: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', ts) AS t, outcome AS series, COUNT(*) AS value FROM "iris.provisioning" WHERE COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}} GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Provisioning latency by accelerator
panels.description: Create-to-ready time for slices that came up, by accelerator variant. Climbing latency precedes stockouts.

params.value: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', ts) AS t, CASE WHEN accelerator_variant = '' THEN resource_type ELSE accelerator_variant END AS series, AVG(provision_latency_ms) AS value FROM "iris.provisioning" WHERE outcome = 'ready' AND provision_latency_ms > 0 AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}} GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Waiting tasks by job
panels.description: Tasks not yet running, per selected root job. With every job selected this is the fleet's backlog by job; narrow the job selector and it becomes one job's own queue over time.

params.value: SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', ts) AS t, root_job_id AS series, MAX(pending + assigned + building) AS value FROM "iris.task_state" WHERE root_job_id IN (${job:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}} GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Active jobs
panels.description: One row per active root job on the selected CoreWeave clusters, newest snapshot within a two-minute window, worst wait first. A finished job stops emitting and ages out rather than lingering here.

params.value: WITH recent AS ( SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') AS cluster, root_job_id, pending, assigned, building, running, oldest_pending_age_ms, oldest_building_age_ms, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "cluster", root_job_id ORDER BY ts DESC) AS rn FROM "iris.task_state" WHERE root_job_id IN (${job:sqlstring}) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}}) SELECT "cluster", root_job_id AS job, pending, assigned, building, running, oldest_pending_age_ms, oldest_building_age_ms FROM recent WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY GREATEST(oldest_building_age_ms, oldest_pending_age_ms) DESC

panels.title: Recent warning events
panels.description: The raw event stream behind the chart above, newest first. Use it after the chart has told you which reason to look at.

params.value: SELECT ts, COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') AS cluster, task_id, attempt_id, reason, source, message, count FROM "iris.task_event" WHERE type = 'Warning' AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}} ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 200

panels.title: marin jobs by state
panels.description: Root-job counts from the marin controller: in flight now, plus terminal states over the trailing 24h. GCE controllers emit no iris.task_state, so they are queried live.

panels.title: marin-dev jobs by state
panels.description: The same counts from the marin-dev controller.

panels.title: Top tasks by memory
panels.description: Twenty highest-memory task attempts on the GCE clusters. iris.task carries no accelerator columns, so this is host memory.

params.value: WITH top AS ( SELECT task_id FROM "iris.task" WHERE ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}} GROUP BY task_id ORDER BY AVG(memory_mb) DESC LIMIT 20) SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', ts) AS t, task_id AS series, AVG(memory_mb) AS value FROM "iris.task" WHERE ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}} AND task_id IN (SELECT task_id FROM top) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Top tasks by CPU
panels.description: Twenty highest-CPU task attempts on the GCE clusters.

params.value: WITH top AS ( SELECT task_id FROM "iris.task" WHERE ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}} GROUP BY task_id ORDER BY AVG(cpu_millicores) DESC LIMIT 20) SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', ts) AS t, task_id AS series, AVG(cpu_millicores) AS value FROM "iris.task" WHERE ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}} AND task_id IN (SELECT task_id FROM top) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Top workers by host CPU
panels.description: Twenty busiest GCE workers by host CPU.

params.value: WITH top AS ( SELECT worker_id FROM "iris.worker" WHERE ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}} GROUP BY worker_id ORDER BY AVG(cpu_pct) DESC LIMIT 20) SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', ts) AS t, worker_id AS series, AVG(cpu_pct) AS value FROM "iris.worker" WHERE ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}} AND worker_id IN (SELECT worker_id FROM top) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

WITH top AS ( SELECT worker_id FROM "iris.worker" WHERE ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}} GROUP BY worker_id ORDER BY AVG(mem_bytes) DESC LIMIT 20) SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '${__interval_ms} milliseconds', ts) AS t, worker_id AS series, AVG(mem_bytes) AS value FROM "iris.worker" WHERE ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}} AND worker_id IN (SELECT worker_id FROM top) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1
